description.detailed_description: The image shows a urine dipstick being held next to a reference chart for color comparison. The dipstick has multiple colored pads, each corresponding to a specific test parameter (e.g., pH, protein, glucose). A urine sample container with a pink lid is visible in the background, slightly out of focus. The setup suggests a qualitative or semi-quantitative analysis of urine components.

Case_18018/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: Double disk synergy test and combined-disk test with Imipenem alone (A) and with EDTA disk tests (B). The picture shows a combined disk test that uses the disk of imipenem alone (IMP) and the disk of imipenem plus EDTA (IMP-EDTA). An enhanced inhibition zone of more than 7 mm around IMP + EDTA is seen when a metallo-beta-lactamase is present.

description.short_caption: Double disk synergy test showing enhanced inhibition with IMP + EDTA disk.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a culture plate with two disks labeled 'IMP' (imipenem alone) and 'IMP + EDTA' (imipenem plus EDTA). The plate demonstrates a clear enhancement of the inhibition zone around the IMP + EDTA disk compared to the IMP disk alone. This finding is consistent with the presence of a metallo-beta-lactamase enzyme, which is inhibited by EDTA. The test is a combined disk test used to detect metallo-beta-lactamase production in bacterial isolates.
visible_findings: enhanced inhibition zone around 'IMP + EDTA' disk
